meta.source: ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (2025-01-15), Part 1 - Writing rules, summary of the rules for each section

check_levels.auto: The script checks this rule fully.
check_levels.partial: The script finds common violations. The agent must still review the text for this rule.
check_levels.manual: The script can not check this rule. The agent must review the text for this rule.

rules.statement: Use words that are: approved in the dictionary, technical nouns, technical verbs.
rules.agent_hint: If the checker reports a word as unknown, either replace it with an approved word or, if it is a real technical noun or technical verb for your subject field, add it to data/technical_names.txt or data/technical_verbs.txt.

rules.statement: Use approved words from the dictionary only as the specified part of speech.
rules.agent_hint: Run `lookup` on a word to see which part of speech is approved. Example: CHECK is an approved noun, but not an approved verb (use MAKE SURE, EXAMINE or MEASURE).

rules.statement: Use approved words only with their approved meanings.
rules.agent_hint: Run `lookup` and compare the 'meaning' field with how you use the word. If your meaning is different, use the alternative that the dictionary gives.

rules.statement: Use only the approved forms of verbs and adjectives.
rules.agent_hint: Only the forms listed in the dictionary entry are approved (for example ADJUST, ADJUSTS, ADJUSTED). Comparative forms of adjectives are approved only if listed.

rules.statement: You can use words that you can include in a technical noun category.
rules.agent_hint: Technical nouns are names of items, materials, locations, processes, measurements and similar (22 categories in the standard). Keep the project list in data/technical_names.txt.

rules.statement: Use a word that is not approved in the dictionary, only when it is a technical noun or part of a technical noun.
rules.agent_hint: A not-approved word is allowed only inside a technical noun (for example 'fuel line', not 'line up').

rules.statement: Do not use words that are technical nouns as verbs.
rules.agent_hint: Write 'apply oil to the bearing', not 'oil the bearing'.

rules.statement: Use technical nouns that are approved in your company, industry, or subject field.
When you must select a technical noun, use one which is short and easy to understand.
Do not use regional, slang, or jargon words as technical nouns.
Do not use different technical nouns for the same item.
rules.agent_hint: Keep one name per item in data/technical_names.txt and use only that name.

rules.statement: You can use verbs that you can include in a technical verb category.
rules.agent_hint: Technical verbs are verbs for manufacturing processes, computer processes and similar subject-field actions (for example 'machine', 'ream', 'download'). Keep the project list in data/technical_verbs.txt.

rules.statement: Do not use technical verbs as nouns.
Use American English spelling unless other official directives tell you differently.
Write multi-word nouns of no more than three words.
rules.agent_hint: Break long noun groups with prepositions: 'the pressure of the hydraulic fluid in the main valve', not 'main valve hydraulic fluid pressure'.

rules.statement: When a technical noun has more than three words, write it in full.
rules.agent_hint: An official technical noun with more than three words is permitted. Add it to data/technical_names.txt so the checker does not report it.

rules.statement: Use only the verb forms that are given in the dictionary.

Use only these verb forms and tenses of verbs: the infinitive form, the imperative form (command form), the simple present tense, the simple past tense, the simple future tense, the past participle form (as an adjective).
rules.agent_hint: Not permitted: present perfect (has removed), past perfect (had removed), progressive (is removing), conditional (would remove).

rules.statement: Use the past participle form as an adjective.
Do not use auxiliary verbs to make complex verb constructions.
Use the "-ing" form of a verb only as a technical noun or as a modifier in a technical noun.
rules.agent_hint: Permitted: 'landing gear', 'mounting bracket' (technical nouns). Not permitted: 'before installing the unit' (write 'before you install the unit').

rules.statement: Use the active voice. In descriptive writing, you can use the passive voice only when the agent is unknown.
rules.agent_hint: Procedures: always active. Descriptive text: rewrite in the active voice unless you do not know who or what does the action.

rules.statement: Use an approved verb to describe an action, not a noun or other parts of speech.
rules.agent_hint: Write 'install the unit', not 'do the installation of the unit'.

rules.statement: Write short and clear sentences.
Do not omit words or use contractions to make your sentences shorter.
rules.agent_hint: No contractions (don't, it's). Do not leave out articles, verbs or 'that' to save words.

rules.statement: Use a vertical list for complex texts.
Use connecting words and connecting phrases to connect sentences that contain related topics.
When applicable, use an article (the, a, an) or a demonstrative adjective (this, these) before a noun or a multi-word noun.
Write short sentences. Use a maximum of 20 words in each sentence.
rules.agent_hint: Word count follows rules 8.4 to 8.7.

rules.statement: Write only one instruction in each sentence unless two or more actions occur at the same time.
Write instructions in the imperative (command) form.
When there is a condition that the reader must know about first, start the instruction with a descriptive statement. Then, divide that descriptive statement from the command with a comma.
rules.agent_hint: 'If the pressure is more than 50 kPa, open the valve.'

rules.statement: Write notes only to give information, not instructions.
Give information gradually.
Use key words and key phrases to give your text a logical structure.
Write short sentences. Use a maximum of 25 words in each sentence.
Use paragraphs to show related information.
Make sure that each paragraph has only one topic.
Make sure that no paragraph has more than six sentences.
Use an applicable word (for example, "warning" or "caution") to identify the level of risk.
rules.agent_hint: WARNING: risk of injury or death. CAUTION: risk of damage to equipment. Start the safety instruction with this word and a colon.

rules.statement: Start a safety instruction with a clear and accurate command or condition.
Give an explanation to show the risk or possible result.
rules.agent_hint: After the command, add a short sentence that tells the risk: 'IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THIS PRECAUTION, INJURY CAN OCCUR.'

rules.statement: You can use all standard English punctuation marks but not the semicolon (;).
Use hyphens (-) to connect words that are directly related.

You can use parentheses: to make references to illustrations or text; to include letters or numbers that identify items on an illustration or in a text; to identify the work steps in a procedure; to include abbreviations; to give the singular and plural forms of a noun at the same time; to explain words or a part of a sentence; to include an alternative.
In a vertical list, a colon (:) has the same effect on word count as a period and shows the end of a sentence.
When you put text in parentheses, it counts as one word in that sentence.

Count each of these elements as one word: numbers; numbers together with units of measurement; abbreviations; alphanumeric identifiers; quoted text; titles, headings, placards, and labels; proper nouns of individuals, groups, organizations, and geopolitical entities.
Hyphenated words count as one word.
Use a different sentence construction to write a sentence when a word-for-word replacement is not sufficient.
Use each approved word correctly.
When you use two words together, do not make phrasal verbs.
rules.agent_hint: Write 'start', not 'turn on' (unless the dictionary approves it); write 'do', not 'carry out'.

rules.statement: When you select terminology or wording, always use a consistent style.
The conjunction "that": do not leave it out after verbs such as "make sure" and "show".
The preposition "with": use it only with its approved meanings.
How to use pronouns: make sure that each pronoun refers clearly to one item.
The pronoun "this": make sure that the reader knows the item it refers to.
False friends: be careful with words that look like words in another language but have a different meaning.
Latin abbreviations: do not use them (e.g., i.e., etc.). Use English words.
Inclusive language: use neutral and non-discriminatory terms.
Possessive form: it is permitted, but if you are not sure that the sentence is correct, do not use it.
